[m51] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

[m1] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: (top of page) | text
Changing your position on the road involves changing lanes or overtaking and passing another vehicle.

[m4] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: (top of page) | text
Before beginning, be sure you have enough space and time to complete the move safely.

[m2] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Passing is changing lanes to move past a slower vehicle.

[m3] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. For example, cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are usually slower than the through traffic. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

[m5] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Never overtake and pass another vehicle unless you are sure you can do so without danger to yourself or others.

[m72] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Don't pass moving snow plows under any conditions.

[m6] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
If in doubt, do not pass.

[m8] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Here are the steps for passing a vehicle:

[m9] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Use your left-turn signal to show that you want to pass and check that the way is clear ahead and behind before moving into the passing lane.

[m10] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Watch for bicycles and small vehicles that may be hidden from view in front of the vehicle you are about to pass. Also watch for vehicles that may be turning left in front of you and vehicles or pedestrians entering the road from another road or driveway.

[m11] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Change lanes only after signalling. After overtaking, signal that you want to move back into the lane you started from, and when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you are passing in your inside mirror, make the lane change.

[m12] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Be careful not to cut off a vehicle by suddenly moving in front of it.

[m13] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
If the vehicle you are passing speeds up, do not race. Go back to your original lane.

[m85] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
And do not speed up when another driver is trying to pass you. It is unlawful and dangerous.

[m14] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | figure
Figure: Diagram 2-46 | Alt text: “how to pass another vehicle”

[m15] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Passing within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover is not permitted.

[m17] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Passing left of a centreline is not permitted 30 metres from a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

[m18] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
Don't attempt to pass when approaching the crest of a hill or on a curve where your vision of oncoming traffic is obstructed and there is not enough clear distance ahead to pass in safety.

[m50] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
When passing parked vehicles, watch carefully for people suddenly opening doors or for doors opened to load and unload.

[m84] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
When faster traffic wants to pass you, move to the right and let it pass in safety.

[m89] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

[m90] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | text
On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

[m52] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing | figure
Figure: Diagram 2-47 | Alt text: “how to pass another vehicle”

[m39] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing at night | text
Be very careful when you pass other vehicles at night.

[m40] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing at night | text
If you have to pass and the way is clear, follow these steps:

[m41] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing at night | text
Switch your headlights to low beams as you approach a vehicle from behind.

[m42] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing at night | text
Signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and pull out to pass. As you move alongside the vehicle you are passing, switch on your high beams. This will let you see more of the road ahead.

[m43] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing at night | text
When you can see all of the front of the vehicle you are passing in your rear view mirror, you are far enough ahead to pull back into the right lane. Remember to signal.

[m27] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing and climbing lanes | figure
Figure: Diagram 2-48 | Alt text: “a passing or climbing lane”

[m28] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing and climbing lanes | text
Some roads have special passing or climbing lanes. These lanes let slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so that faster ones can pass safely in the left lane.

[m29] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing and climbing lanes | text
An advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass. Another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane.

[m38] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing on the shoulder | text
You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved. You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

[m35] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing on the right | text
Most passing is done on the left. You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

[m36] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing on the right | text
Passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left.

[m37] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing on the right | text
If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right. Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.

[m61] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing streetcars | figure
Figure: Diagram 2-49 | Alt text: “a vehicle stopped the required two metres behind the rear doors of a stopped streetcar”

[m62] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing streetcars | text
You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road.

[m63] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing streetcars | text
At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.

[m64] page: Changing positions page · Chapter 2 | heading: Passing streetcars | text
Always pass these areas at a reasonable speed and be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves.

statements.text: DEFINE changing position IS a manoeuvre THAT changes lanes OR passes another vehicle

sources.quote: Changing your position on the road involves changing lanes or overtaking and passing another vehicle.

statements.text: DEFINE passing IS a lane change THAT moves past a slower vehicle ALSO CALLED overtaking

sources.quote: Passing is changing lanes to move past a slower vehicle.

flags.note: The handbook uses "pass", "overtake" and "overtake and pass" for the same manoeuvre.

statements.text: FACT vehicles on the same road do not all travel at the same speed, even though every public road has a speed limit

sources.quote: While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. For example, cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are usually slower than the through traffic. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

statements.text: FACT cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers preparing to turn are [?usually] slower than through traffic

sources.quote: While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. For example, cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are usually slower than the through traffic. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

flags.note: Hedged generalisation.

statements.note: "You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles" is motivation, not a permission, so no MAY rule is written for it.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD start a lane change or a pass ONLY IF the driver has [?enough] space and time to complete it [?safely]

sources.quote: Before beginning, be sure you have enough space and time to complete the move safely.

flags.note: No measure of space or time.
Judgment term.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle UNLESS the driver is [?sure] the pass can be made without danger to the driver or others

sources.quote: Never overtake and pass another vehicle unless you are sure you can do so without danger to yourself or others.

flags.note: Subjective certainty; no observable test.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN the driver is [?in doubt]

sources.quote: If in doubt, do not pass.

flags.note: Subjective state; the catch-all behind 2.1b.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle

sources.quote: Here are the steps for passing a vehicle:
how to pass another vehicle

flags.note: Called "rear view mirror" in the night procedure (3.3.1b).

statements.note: Steps 1 and 2 restate the lane-change steps on the same page; the order of the steps carries "only after signalling".

steps.text: signal left AND check that the way is clear ahead and behind
WATCH FOR bicycles and small vehicles hidden in front of the vehicle being passed, vehicles turning left ahead, and vehicles or pedestrians entering from a road or driveway
signal right to return to the original lane
move back into the original lane WHEN the entire front of the vehicle being passed is visible in the inside mirror
IF the vehicle being passed speeds up THEN do not race AND go back to the original lane

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut off the vehicle being passed by moving in front of it suddenly WHEN returning to the original lane

sources.quote: Be careful not to cut off a vehicle by suddenly moving in front of it.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass [?on the left of a centreline] WHEN the driver is [?30 m from] a bridge, viaduct or tunnel

sources.quote: Passing left of a centreline is not permitted 30 metres from a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

flags.note: "30 metres from" is read as "within 30 m of"; the text does not say whether it covers both approaches.

flags.span: on the left of a centreline
flags.note: Prohibits the means (crossing the centreline), not passing; passing near a bridge on a multi-lane road is not covered.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN (the driver is approaching the crest of a hill OR the driver is on a curve) AND the view of oncoming traffic is obstructed AND the clear distance ahead is not [?enough] to pass [?safely]

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass when approaching the crest of a hill or on a curve where your vision of oncoming traffic is obstructed and there is not enough clear distance ahead to pass in safety.

flags.note: No distance given.
Judgment term.

statements.text: DEFINE a passing lane or climbing lane IS an added lane THAT lets slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so faster vehicles can pass [?safely] in the left lane

sources.quote: Some roads have special passing or climbing lanes. These lanes let slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so that faster ones can pass safely in the left lane.
a passing or climbing lane

flags.note: Judgment term inside a definition.

statements.text: FACT an advance sign tells drivers a passing opportunity is coming, AND another sign warns when the added lane is ending

sources.quote: An advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass. Another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane.

statements.force_from: implied ("so drivers … can begin to merge safely")
statements.text: a driver in the right-hand lane SHOULD merge [?safely] with traffic in the left-hand lane WHEN a sign warns that the lane is ending

sources.quote: An advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass. Another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane.

flags.note: The rule is implied by a purpose clause about the sign; the text states no instruction.
Judgment term.

statements.force_from: default (stated as a description: "Most passing is done on the left")
statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass on the left BECAUSE passing on the right can be more dangerous

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left. You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.
Passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left.

flags.note: The default is described, not instructed; it is needed so that 3.2.3b reads as an exception.
Hedged generalisation in the source.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO 3.2.3a: a driver MAY pass on the right WHEN the road is multi-lane OR the road is one-way OR the vehicle being passed is a streetcar OR the vehicle being passed is turning left

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left. You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD wait WHEN the driver is in the leftmost lane with a slower vehicle in front UNTIL the slower vehicle moves to the right

sources.quote: If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right. Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT change lanes suddenly to pass on the right WHEN the driver is in the leftmost lane behind a slower vehicle BECAUSE the driver in front may move to the right at the same time

sources.quote: If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right. Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.

statements.text: a driver MAY drive on the right shoulder ONLY IF the driver is passing a vehicle that is turning left AND the shoulder is paved

sources.quote: You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved. You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

flags.note: Presupposes that driving on the shoulder is otherwise not allowed; that default is not stated here.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass on the left shoulder, whether or not it is paved

sources.quote: You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved. You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass with [?extra care] WHEN it is night

sources.quote: Be very careful when you pass other vehicles at night.

flags.note: A caution with no named hazard, so WATCH FOR does not fit.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle at night SPECIALIZES 2.2a WHEN the driver has to pass AND the way is clear

sources.quote: If you have to pass and the way is clear, follow these steps:

flags.note: The handbook calls the mirror "rear view mirror" here and "inside mirror" in 2.2a; both rules say inside mirror.

steps.text: switch to low beams WHILE approaching the vehicle from behind
signal, check the mirrors and blind spot, AND pull out to pass
switch on high beams WHILE alongside the vehicle being passed BECAUSE this shows more of the road ahead
move back into the original lane AND signal WHEN the entire front of the vehicle being passed is visible in the inside mirror

statements.text: a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR doors opening suddenly AND doors opened to load or unload WHILE passing parked vehicles

sources.quote: When passing parked vehicles, watch carefully for people suddenly opening doors or for doors opened to load and unload.

statements.text: FACT motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds [?often] move to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions OR to be seen

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

flags.note: Hedged generalisation.

statements.force_from: imperative ("Do not take this as an invitation")
statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped within its lane BECAUSE its position in the lane is not an invitation to pass (3.4.2a)

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.
how to pass another vehicle

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes WHEN passing a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

statements.text: a driver MUST pass a streetcar on the right UNLESS the driver is on a one-way road

sources.quote: You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay at least 2 m behind the rear doors of a streetcar WHEN the streetcar is stopped AND passengers are getting on or off

sources.quote: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.
a vehicle stopped the required two metres behind the rear doors of a stopped streetcar

flags.note: The diagram's alt text calls it "the required two metres", which suggests a legal requirement.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO 3.4.5b WHEN the streetcar stop has an area set aside for passengers

sources.quote: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass a streetcar passenger area at a [?reasonable speed] AND SHOULD WATCH FOR pedestrians making sudden or unexpected moves

sources.quote: Always pass these areas at a reasonable speed and be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves.

flags.note: No speed given.
The source says "these areas"; read as the passenger areas in 3.4.5c.
Repeated on the pedestrians page, with an added caution about sudden moves.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a snow plow WHEN the snow plow is moving

sources.quote: Don't pass moving snow plows under any conditions.

flags.note: Absolute wording ("under any conditions") without a legal marker; the default gives SHOULD NOT.

statements.text: a driver being passed MUST NOT speed up WHILE another driver is trying to pass BECAUSE it is dangerous

sources.quote: And do not speed up when another driver is trying to pass you. It is unlawful and dangerous.

statements.text: a driver being passed SHOULD WATCH FOR oncoming traffic AND SHOULD move closer to the right side of the lane WHEN on an undivided road AND the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane

sources.quote: When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

statements.text: a driver being passed SHOULD be ready to slow down WHEN on an undivided road AND the passing driver is in the opposite lane BECAUSE slowing down lets the passing driver get back in front sooner and prevents a collision

sources.quote: When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

statements.text: a driver in the truck passing lane SHOULD move into the right-hand lane [?as soon as the driver can] WHEN a truck wants to pass

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

flags.span: as soon as the driver can
flags.note: No time given (the handbook says "as soon as you can").
